pickthall.translator: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain

verses.text: By the snorting courses
Striking sparks of fire
And scouring to the raid at dawn
Then, therewith, with their trail of dust
Cleaving, as one, the centre (of the foe)
Lo! man is an ingrate unto his Lord
And lo! he is a witness unto that
And lo! in the love of wealth he is violent
Knoweth he not that, when the contents of the graves are poured forth
And the secrets of the breasts are made known
On that day will their Lord be perfectly informed concerning them

yusufali.translator: Abdullah Yusuf Ali, The Holy Quran (1934), public domain

verses.text: By the (Steeds) that run, with panting (breath)
And strike sparks of fire
And push home the charge in the morning
And raise the dust in clouds the while
And penetrate forthwith into the midst (of the foe) en masse
Truly man is, to his Lord, ungrateful
And to that (fact) he bears witness (by his deeds)
And violent is he in his love of wealth
Does he not know,- when that which is in the graves is scattered abroad
And that which is (locked up) in (human) breasts is made manifest
That their Lord had been Well-acquainted with them, (even to) that Day
